The Code of Corporate Ethics (hereinafter referred to as the Code) establishes the internal rules applicable to the Personnel of the International Investment Bank (hereinafter referred to as the MIB and Bank). It defines the Bank's corporate values and principles and sets professional and ethical standards expected from the Personnel.  The provisions of the Code shall apply to all Bank staff. ### persons working in the IAB within the framework of the internship programme; ### persons providing services to the IAB in accordance with civil law treaties.  ### 1.1.3. The Code is a tool for the use of the Bank's employees in their daily activities. The development of the Code and its further integration into the Bank's daily activities is one of the most important tasks in the development of corporate culture and the improvement of the efficiency of the work of the Staff, as well as in the processes aimed at preventing potential losses and reducing risks.  ### 1.1.4. The Code establishes the core corporate values, rules of conduct based on high professional and ethical standards, which the activities of the Bank's employees regardless of their positions must comply with.  ### 1.1.5. The Code establishes general principles that correspond to the Bank's values such as partnership, efficiency and business reputation. Some of the Code's rules aimed at identifying conflicts of interest involve consideration of situations and the provision of information by the Employees about close relatives.  The Code aims to introduce the common values that define the unique image of the Bank into the Bank's corporate life and business relations with all stakeholders.  ### 1.1.7. The Code's tasks include:  - the introduction of corporate values, the observance of which will contribute to the achievement of the Bank's strategic objectives and mission; - establish norms that will help employees determine their behaviour in areas of daily activity where potential conflicts of interest may arise; - providing recommendations and explanations regarding the interpretation and application of ethical values and principles; - ensuring a common understanding of the risks and threats to the Bank's activities arising from the employees' corporate behaviour. ### 1.1.8. The Bank welcomes the open discussion of the provisions of the Code by all Employees, as well as the interaction aimed at making changes or additions to the Code. The Code shall be approved by the Board of Directors of the Bank and further revised as necessary (at least once every five years). 1.1.10. This document may be disclosed to third parties only in accordance with the Regulations. ### 1.1.11. The list of the Bank's current Regulatory Documents which expire with the adoption of this document is given in Section 5.  ### 1.1.12. Structural unit responsible for the development and timely updating of the document: Compliance Department. ## 1.2. **Terms and definitions**  ## Below is a list of terms and definitions adopted under the Code.  The International Investment Bank, including its branches and representative offices. ### 2.3.1. The Bank shall ensure the effectiveness of decisions by comprehensively checking and evaluating the potential benefits and risks, taking into account the Bank's mission and the interests of the Bank's member countries. ### 2.3.2. The Bank shall endeavour to use its available resources in the most efficient and rational manner to contribute to the maximum fulfilment of its Mandate. The mandate of the Bank shall be determined by the IAB's Founding Documents, in particular by the Bank's prior long-term objectives and the powers conferred on the Bank to achieve them.
